info.desc: The Downward Spiral (also known as Halo 8) is Nine Inch Nails' second studio album, though it is largely considered the third major release after the Broken EP, which consisted of entirely new material. It was released on March 8, 1994. It is likely the most acclaimed and well-known of the band's discography, and is said to have brought "industrial" music to the mainstream. A collection featuring remixes from The Downward Spiral was released as Further Down The Spiral on June 1, 1995. podcast.body: Released in 1994, this album by Nine Inch Nails is characterized by its diverse and often chaotic sounds, with unexpected appearances of piano elements integrated amidst the noise. It showcases how Reznor's piano compositions and manipulations contribute to the album's sonic landscape. "For example, let's go to 1994's The Downward Spiral. Other sounds are all over this album, popping up when you least expect it, like in this song."

podcast.body: This Nine Inch Nails album, released in 1994, was Trent Reznor's primary project at the time, but during its sessions, the idea for the collaborative side project Tapeworm was conceived. Tapeworm was intended to be an outlet for other band members to contribute as equals, distinct from Reznor's control over NIN. "The idea for tapeworm went as far back as the sessions for the downward spiral in 1994. Now that was Trent's project."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album was recorded in a house at 10,050 Cielo Drive in Benedict Canyon, Los Angeles, which Trent Reznor rented in July 1992. Unbeknownst to Trent at the time of signing the rental agreement, this was the site of the Manson family murders in 1969. The studio gear, installed over three months, was set up in the very room where Sharon Tate and Jay Sebring were murdered. Equipment mysteriously and frequently broke down. Trent named this temporary studio "Le Pig," and the word "pig" features prominently on the album, referencing the word written in Sharon Tate's blood on the living room wall by the Manson family. Trent described the recording period as "the blackest, the bleakest," stating, "I hate what I do. I don't like doing it anymore."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album was released by Nine Inch Nails, three weeks prior to Trent Reznor's contribution of a cover of Joy Division's "Dead Souls" to *The Crow* soundtrack in 1994. The album was described as "long-awaited," indicating its high anticipation among fans. "And Trent Resner, who released the long-awaited Nine-inch Nails album The Downward Spiral just three weeks earlier, contributed this stunning version of Joy Division's Dead Souls."

podcast.body: This album, released in 1994, contains the original song "Hurt," which was later famously covered by Johnny Cash. "It features material written by Paul Simon, DePesh Mode, Sting, The Beatles, The Eagles, A duet with Nick Cave, and most importantly, a rendition of Hurt, from the 9-inch nails album The Downward Spiral."

podcast.body: This highly anticipated second album was released on June 29, 1994, about six weeks before their Woodstock '94 performance. Due to immense pent-up demand, it debuted on the charts at number two. "The pent-up demand was huge. And the album entered the charts at number two."

podcast.title: Accusations of Theft
podcast.body: This album was released in 1994 and became the subject of a plagiarism lawsuit from Mark Anofrio, who claimed five songs ("Closer," "Hurt," "March of the Pigs," "Mr. Self-destruct," and "Downward Spiral") were stolen from his "Elephant Man" compositions. "Then in 1994, Anofrio said that he was shocked to find that five songs in the downward spiral sounded suspiciously similar to his Elephant Man compositions."

podcast.title: Breakthrough Album
podcast.body: Released two years after the "Broken" EP, this album marked a turning point for Nine Inch Nails, propelling Trent Reznor into widespread success. After its release, Trent's career took off with extensive tours, remixing projects, producing gigs, and the growth of his Nothing Records label. The period from "The Downward Spiral" onwards is described as well-documented, contrasting with the more obscure early years. "Two years after Broken came out, the downward spiral. And from that point, Trent Resner has really never looked back."

podcast.title: Piano Elements Amidst Chaos
podcast.body: Released in 1994, this album is notable for its dynamic soundscape, often featuring unexpected piano elements that emerge from the band's characteristic chaos and noise. It highlights how Trent Reznor's classical piano background subtly influences the album's diverse sonic textures. "For example, let's go to 1994's The Downward Spiral. Other sounds are all over this album, popping up when you least expect it, like in this song."

podcast.title: Recorded at Sharon Tate Murder House; Reached #2 in US
podcast.body: Trent Reznor recorded NIN's second album in a house at 10050 Cielo Drive in the Bel Air area of Los Angeles — the same property where Charles Manson's followers murdered actress Sharon Tate and her friends on August 9, 1969. The murders were so brutal they still resonated through LA culture decades later. Reznor was descending into depression, alcoholism, and drug addiction during recording. The album used cutting-edge digital techniques and hardware. Despite being an intensely heavy industrial record, it reached number two on the Billboard album chart, was top 10 in the UK, and eventually sold north of five million copies worldwide. Many consider it the best Nine Inch Nails album ever made and one of the greatest albums of the 1990s. "It was a testament to how popular alt-rock had become that this heavy industrial record reached number two."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: After enduring record label hell for a couple of years, Trent Reznor was finally free to start work on his second album, using the process as a form of self-therapy to explore serious psychic scars from that period. He rented a house in Hollywood, set up a studio, and began work, later discovering it was the site of the Charles Manson murders of Sharon Tate and her friends in 1969, a realization that affected the album especially after an unexpected meeting with Sharon Tate's sister. While lacking a straightforward narrative, the album is thematically cohesive, delving into Trent's feelings about religion, relationships, career, self-destruction, and the very sense of being. The content was so intense and personal that a song titled "Just and Do It," which leaned too far towards encouraging suicide, was removed. "He called this album The Downward Spiral, and while there's no straightforward narrative or story, the album holds together thematically."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album by Nine Inch Nails, led by Trent Reznor, is cited as a work that would not have been possible without the extensive use of distortion and feedback. It exemplifies Reznor's ongoing experimentation with taming noise in his music since the 1980s. "An album like The Downward Spiral would not have been possible without distortion and feedback."
